messages:
anya: hey team, quick onboarding question — what's the recommended pattern for using Redwood keys in local dev + CI? i'm worried about committing keys or getting 429s in CI when many e2e jobs run concurrently.
mira: welcome aboard :wave: TL;DR: never put hosted prod keys in public repos or shared CI envs. use sandbox keys for casual dev, and for CI use per-repo service tokens stored in our SecretsManager with least privilege.
anya: thanks! how different are sandbox quotas vs hosted? curious if sandbox 429s are expected during demos.
devon: sandbox is rate-limited and much lower concurrency than hosted. expect lower token/sec and lower burst limits. for demos we either: 1) request a temporary hosted dev key for the team (short-lived, explain RPS), or 2) mock the API with recorded responses.
anya: how do i open a request for a temporary hosted dev key? any template?
devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood.devex/keys-and-quotas — contains the "Temporary Dev Keys" section and the quota request form: https://internal.redwood.devex/requests/keys. Policy: include team name, reason, expected concurrency, duration, and whether streaming is needed.
sam: small snippet for CI best-practices: put the token in SecretsManager, reference it in CI as SECRET_RW_KEY, and never echo it. Example in GitHub Actions:
```
- name: Set RW key
  run: echo "RW_KEY=$GITHUB_SECRET_RW_KEY" >> $GITHUB_ENV
- name: Run tests
  env:
    RW_KEY: ${{ secrets.SECRET_RW_KEY }}
  run: pytest tests/e2e --max-workers=2
```
We throttle parallel workers in CI to avoid 429s. Also add retry/backoff for transient 429s.
anya: is there an endpoint to check remaining quota so tests can skip heavy suites if near limit?
mira: yes — account limits endpoint. You can check headers like X-RateLimit-Remaining on responses or call GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/limits for a summary. We also surface limits in the Console.
anya: perfect. one more: for streaming tests, sandbox behaves differently?
devon: streaming is supported but sandbox has lower concurrent stream count. If you need many concurrent streaming sessions for a demo, request the temporary hosted dev key and specify streaming. Otherwise, use a recorder tool that plays back streaming chunks locally.
anya: got it, i'll set up per-repo secret for CI and open a temporary hosted key request for our demo next week. appreciate the help! :smile:
